body: Addition can describe joining collections with no shared members. Joining a pair of marks and three more marks gives five: 2 + 3 = 5. Equality says that both sides represent the same value. Removing a group of three from the five leaves two: 5 − 3 = 2.

Multiplication can count equally sized groups: three groups of four objects contain twelve objects. Dividing twelve into groups of four gives three groups. Dividing five whole objects into two equally sized groups leaves one object over if the objects are kept whole.
credit: Centauri Archive editorial draft, written with AI assistance
limitations: These examples use whole objects. Fractions and negative numbers extend the operations to other cases. Division by zero has no defined value in ordinary arithmetic.
purpose: Show how operations change quantities while preserving checkable relationships.
